score.title: How a restaurant's score is calculated
score.body: The score shown on a restaurant page isn't a simple average of every review. It uses a damped-average formula: the more reviews a restaurant has, the more its score reflects the real experience there; a brand-new restaurant with only one or two reviews gets pulled toward the sitewide average, so a couple of extreme early reviews (too harsh or too generous) can't swing the score on their own.
score.calloutBody: A brand-new restaurant rated 5 stars a few times by friends shouldn't automatically top the rankings. This formula makes scores more trustworthy while a restaurant still has few reviews, and lets them settle into the real experience as more people rate it.

axes.title: The 7 rating criteria
axes.body: Alongside the overall rating, reviewers can also rate 7 individual criteria — shown as a breakdown chart on the restaurant page so you can see where a place is strong or weak. These criteria are not factored into the overall score at the top of the page — that score comes only from the overall rating. Reviewers can skip any criterion they didn't experience.

space.label: Atmosphere
space.note: Noise level, seating, lighting, how open the space feels.

price.label: Price
price.note: How the price compares to what you get.

service.label: Service
service.note: Attitude, how fast orders come out, handling mistakes.

hygiene.label: Cleanliness
hygiene.note: Tables, utensils, and any visible prep area.

wifi.label: Wifi
wifi.note: Only applies when the restaurant has wifi.

parking.label: Parking
parking.note: Whether there's space, an attendant, or a fee.

moderation.title: How reviews get moderated
moderation.body: The goal is keeping reviews real, not keeping a restaurant's score flattering.

1.title: Signed-in users only
1.body: Each account can only re-review the same restaurant after a minimum of 24 hours since its last review, to limit spam.

2.title: Automatic filtering
2.body: Every review gets a risk score (ad links, spam phrases, rapid-fire posting…) — high-risk reviews are held for a moderator to check before they go live.

3.title: Community reports
3.body: Anyone can report a review or incorrect restaurant information; the moderation team reviews it and decides.

data.title: Where the data comes from
data.body: Restaurant information is contributed and kept current by the community. Opening hours, phone numbers, and facilities can change — if you spot something wrong, submit an update right from the restaurant page in the mobile app.
data.source1Body: ratings, photos, comments, and status reports (hours changed, closed down, wrong info) on existing restaurants.
data.source2Body: anyone can add a restaurant that's not on the map yet — a quick moderation check runs before it goes live.
data.disclaimer: Restaurant data shown here may not yet cover every restaurant in Ho Chi Minh City — the system grows as the community contributes.
